title: A repeat small-business refund can verify prior payment acceptance without proving the new payment or restored operating security
source_unit: FTC Yellowstone Capital merchant cash advance refund program and third-payment route
geography: United States small businesses affected by Yellowstone Capital merchant cash advances

observations.period: June 2026 third refund distribution; official page rechecked September 25, 2026

denominator.unit: small businesses receiving a third refund check after cashing a previous check

third_distribution_total.unit: more than U.S. dollars distributed in the third round

prior_payment_condition.value: all reported third-distribution recipients had cashed a previous refund check

earlier_cashed_population.unit: businesses reported by the FTC 2024 annual refund report as having cashed at least one payment

august_2024_cashed_population.unit: businesses reported as cashing the August 2024 additional distribution

underlying_exposure.value: FTC alleged Yellowstone withdrew money from business bank accounts after businesses had repaid the full amounts owed in merchant cash advance contracts

third_check_receipt_and_recovery.unit: missing third-check delivery or cashing, individual amount, account correction, residual loss, business survival, employment, customer continuity, and later financing choice

mechanism.value: Prior check cashing creates a stronger reachability signal for a repeat remedy while leaving the new payment and durable business recovery unobserved

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official FTC Yellowstone Capital refund page and the FTC 2024 Annual Report on Refunds to Consumers; prior cashing, third-round dispatch, and aggregate historical counts are kept separate from third-check receipt, adequacy, and operating recovery.
observations.uncertainty: The public sources do not provide business identifiers, individual refund amounts, third-check cashing, underlying account correction, remaining loss, operating status, employment, customer continuity, trust, switching, or exit. Aggregate recipient counts are not a business-level recovery rate.
observations.subgroup: Small businesses affected by Yellowstone Capital merchant cash advances, including 3,759 businesses identified as third-distribution recipients; no sector, geography, size, or loss subgroup outcome is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Prior cashing is stronger than a payment offer, but it does not establish that the third check arrived, that the original withdrawal was corrected, or that the business recovered or changed financing.

related_sources.claim: The FTC 2024 annual report records aggregate prior-payment cashing and the August 2024 additional distribution for Yellowstone-affected businesses.

boundary: This record establishes an official repeat-refund route with a prior-cashing condition for small businesses. It does not establish third-payment receipt, adequate recovery, account correction, business survival, trust, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the official FTC refund page and annual report; direct publisher-page retrieval is represented through the retained project ledger and its access boundary.
